title: Chua's circuit (chaotic double-scroll oscillator): topology and verified values
text: Chua's circuit: node V1 holds C1 in parallel with the nonlinear resistor NR (Chua diode) to ground; resistor R joins V1 to node V2; node V2 holds C2 and inductor L in parallel to ground. Values (Kennedy 1992, verified in this Workbench by simulation): C1 = 10 nF, C2 = 100 nF, L = 18 mH, R = 1.8 kOhm (chaotic from about 1.55 to 1.9 kOhm). NR is a piecewise-linear negative conductance: Ga = -0.757 mS inside +-Bp, Gb = -0.409 mS outside, Bp about 1 V. Two NR realizations work here: two op-amp negative impedance converters on the internal solver, or a behavioral_current_source on Xyce (see the Chua NR cards). Observe V(V1) against V(V2) (XY) and add I(L) for XYZ. Verified op-amp sweep: R 1500 rail-limited periodic orbit; 1550-1900 double scroll with a periodic window near 1650; 1950-2000 single scroll; 2050 and above settles to a fixed point.

title: Chua diode from two op-amp negative impedance converters (Kennedy realization)
text: Two opamp_generic op amps, both IN+ on node V1; V+ = +9 V and V- = -9 V on every op amp (supply sources or power ports); headroom 0 (default, output saturates at the rails). A1: 220 Ohm OUT to IN+, 220 Ohm OUT to IN-, 2.2 kOhm IN- to GND (slope -1/2.2k; saturates outside the operating range). A2: 22 kOhm OUT to IN+, 22 kOhm OUT to IN-, 3.3 kOhm IN- to GND (slope -1/3.3k; saturates at about +-1.17 V on V1, the breakpoint). Together Ga = -0.757 mS, Gb = -0.409 mS. Engine: internal solver (opamp_generic has no Xyce model binding). Start with inductor initial_current about 0.1 mA: with a capacitor initial_voltage the internal solver's first step does not converge on this circuit, and with no initial condition it stays on the equilibrium. Transient: step 1 us, stop 50 ms or more, plot from about 20 ms. Verified double scroll at R = 1.8 kOhm.

title: Chua diode as a piecewise-linear behavioral current source (Xyce)
text: Place behavioral_current_source with + on node V1 and - on ground. Its current flows from + through the source to -, so it is the current the nonlinear resistor draws from V1. Value: -0.000409*V(V1)+0.5*(-0.000348)*(abs(V(V1)+1)-abs(V(V1)-1)), which is i = Gb*v + 0.5*(Ga-Gb)*(|v+Bp| - |v-Bp|) with Ga = -0.757 mS, Gb = -0.409 mS, Bp = 1 V. V(name) must be the net's exported name: put a net_label (busName V1) on the node and use that name. Engine: Xyce only (the internal solver refuses behavioral sources). Start with C1 initial_voltage 0.1 V. Verified on Xyce: R 1550-1900 double scroll; 1950-2000 single scroll; 2050 and above a fixed point. This three-segment model has no outer positive slope, so at small R (1500) the solution runs away instead of limiting at rails.

title: Telling chaos from periodic oscillation, decay and numerical trouble
text: Passing ERC or a transient that returns data is not evidence of chaos. Look after the start-up transient (plot from about 20 ms): the signals stay bounded; in Chua's circuit V(C1) jumps between the positive and negative scroll at irregular intervals (many jumps, times between jumps varying by tens of percent); the XY plot of V(C1) against V(C2) fills a double-scroll band instead of retracing one closed loop. Periodic: the XY trace closes on itself and jump intervals repeat. Single scroll: V(C1) stays on one side. Fixed point: the signals go flat. Numerical trouble: values running away, isolated spikes, or a qualitatively different result when the time step is halved; rerun with a smaller step or the other engine. Chaotic time series differ between engines and step sizes by nature; compare the attractor's shape and range, not individual samples.

title: Negative impedance converter (op amp): negative resistance element
text: An op amp with resistor Rf from OUT to IN+ and a divider R2 (OUT to IN-) and R1 (IN- to GND) presents a negative conductance at IN+. In its linear range V_out = V*(1 + R2/R1), so the current into the IN+ node is I = -(R2/(R1*Rf))*V; with R1 = R2 that is -1/Rf. The negative slope holds while the output stays inside the rails, |V| < Vsat*R1/(R1+R2); beyond that the output saturates and the slope becomes +1/Rf. Needs real supplies on V+ and V- (opamp_generic saturates at the rails minus its headroom). The node it drives must be held by a capacitor, inductor or source; on its own the converter is meant to be unstable. Uses: Chua diode, cancelling losses in LC oscillators, negative-resistance oscillators.

title: Piecewise-linear nonlinear element with a behavioral current source
text: behavioral_current_source (pins + and -) takes its current from a Xyce expression in its value. The current flows from + through the source to -; with - on ground it is the current drawn from the + node, so i = f(V(node)) makes any I-V characteristic, i.e. a nonlinear resistor. Piecewise-linear with slope Ga for |v| < Bp and Gb outside: Gb*V(n)+0.5*(Ga-Gb)*(abs(V(n)+Bp)-abs(V(n)-Bp)). Negative slopes make a negative-resistance element. Use V(net) with the net's exported name (name the node with a net_label) and abs(). Behavioral sources run only on the Xyce engine; the internal solver reports this instead of running. behavioral_voltage_source is the voltage counterpart. Look the part up with workbench_capabilities symbolId before setting it.

title: Initial conditions for transient simulation
text: Capacitor initial_voltage (pin 1 relative to pin 2) and inductor initial_current (pin 1 to pin 2) work on both engines; blank means unspecified. A net_label initial_voltage emits .IC for that net and works only on Xyce (the internal solver refuses node initial voltages). Oscillators that start exactly on an equilibrium (symmetric circuits such as Chua's) need a small nonzero initial condition or they never leave it. Check it was used: the first transient samples start at the value set (instrument_plot_data, or the transient trace near t = 0). Known limit: on Chua's op-amp circuit the internal solver fails at its first step with a capacitor initial_voltage; use an inductor initial_current there.

title: 2D/3D plotter: time traces, XY and XYZ phase-space plots
text: Place xyz_plotter (refdes PLOT). Channels A, B, C each have + and - pins: wire + to the node to measure and - to its reference (an unwired - pin is ground). Probes add no load. Set with schematic_set_parameters: mode Time, XY or XYZ; x, y, z signals: a channel letter, V(net), V(net1,net2) or I(part), for example I(L1) for an inductor current; traces (comma separated) for Time mode; stop, step (max time step), start (plot from, to skip start-up); engine Internal or Xyce; markers; projection; x_min to z_max or auto. instrument_read reports samples, ranges, synchronisation and problems such as unwired probes; instrument_plot_data returns the synchronised samples; instrument_open_panel shows the window. Phase portrait: XY with x = voltage across C1, y = voltage across C2; XYZ adds z = I(L).

title: Use workbench_capabilities
text: Tool: workbench_capabilities. Purpose: discover what this Workbench actually has, from its live registries. section components / instruments / analyses / engines (omit for all); query keeps entries containing every word (for example 'behavioral current', 'opamp', 'plot'); symbolId returns one part's pins and parameters with units, choices, defaults and help. Unknown ids come back with close matches. Anything not listed does not exist: do not invent component types, model names or parameters; record a capability_gap instead.
